title: Goa Tour Package Guide: North vs South, Cost & Season
subtitle: How many days you actually need, which half of Goa to stay in, and what a package leaves out.
excerpt: North Goa or South, how many days you actually need, what a package includes and what it leaves out, and when to go — before you compare two quotes.

contentSections.heading: The one decision that shapes a Goa package: North or South
contentSections.content: Most Goa packages run three to six days, and weekend travellers often book 2N/3D. What varies most between operators is not the hotel but how the trip is split. North Goa — Baga, Calangute, Anjuna, Candolim — is where the nightlife, the markets and the water sports are. South Goa — Palolem, Colva, Benaulim — is quieter, less crowded and more resort-shaped. A well-planned package usually gives you a taste of both rather than committing to one side. Group size matters too: couples and small groups tend towards private cabs and boutique stays, families and larger groups towards tempo travellers and mid-range hotels near the main beach belt.
contentSections.highlightQuote: Three to four days covers North Goa properly. If South Goa is also on your list, plan five days or it will feel rushed.

contentSections.heading: Places a Goa package usually covers
contentSections.content: Not every package covers all of these, and the honest ones tell you which are in before you pay.
bulletPoints: Baga and Calangute — the busiest stretch: water sports, beach shacks, nightlife
Candolim and Sinquerim — quieter than Baga, resorts and casual dining
Anjuna and Vagator — flea markets, clifftop viewpoints, a more laid-back crowd
Old Goa — the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Panaji — the state capital, the Fontainhas Latin Quarter and the Mandovi riverfront
Dona Paula and the Mandovi river — where the sunset cruises run from
South Goa beaches — Colva, Benaulim and Palolem, usually added at four days or more
Dudhsagar Waterfalls — a long drive and often a jeep safari through the forest section; best in and just after the monsoon

contentSections.heading: A four-night, five-day Goa shape
contentSections.content: Day 1: arrive, check in, Calangute and Baga Beach, evening free. Day 2: North Goa — Fort Aguada, Candolim Beach, Anjuna, Vagator and Chapora Fort. Day 3: the heritage and southern run — Basilica of Bom Jesus, Se Cathedral, Dona Paula, Miramar and Colva Beach. Day 4: a full day at leisure, with optional water sports or a dolphin trip, and time for the markets. Day 5: breakfast, check-out and the drop at the airport or station. Safar Trails' own Goa trips are linked below and follow this shape, adjusted for your dates and how much of each side you want.

contentSections.heading: Best time to go
contentSections.content: Goa works all year, but the trip changes completely with the season.
bulletPoints: November to February — peak season. Pleasant weather, every shack open, the markets and events running on schedule. Also the most expensive, so book ahead, especially around Christmas and New Year.
March to May — warmer and more humid, but better hotel rates and smaller crowds.
June to September — monsoon. Many shacks close and water sports pause, but the rivers and waterfalls, Dudhsagar included, are at their most dramatic. A greener, quieter trip rather than a beach one.
October — a transition month. The rain tapers off and shacks begin reopening, though the first half can still be unpredictable.

contentSections.heading: How to reach Goa
contentSections.content: By air: Dabolim Airport near Vasco da Gama, and the newer Manohar International Airport (Mopa) in the north. They are at opposite ends of the state, so pick the one that matches where you are staying. By train: the Konkan Railway connects to Mumbai and on towards Mangalore, and the South Western line runs through Madgaon (Margao), which is the station most visitors use. By road: national highways from Mumbai, Pune and Bangalore, with overnight buses a common budget option. Airport or station pickup is arranged as part of the package, along with transport for the rest of the trip.

contentSections.heading: What a Goa package costs
contentSections.content: There is no single fixed price, and any number you see online is a starting point rather than a quote. What actually moves it: the season, since peak (November to February) costs noticeably more than the off-season; the hotel category, where a guesthouse and a four-star beach resort are worlds apart; group size, because per-person cost falls as transport is shared; the number of nights; and the inclusions, since a package with water sports, a cruise or a Dudhsagar day trip built in costs more than a stay-and-sightseeing one. Rather than quote a generic figure, the useful thing is a quote against your real dates and hotel preference.

contentSections.heading: Included, and not included
contentSections.content: Most standard Goa packages include hotel accommodation for the nights booked, breakfast (confirm the exact meal plan), airport or railway station transfers, the local sightseeing in the itinerary, and a private or shared cab depending on the tier. The exclusions are where the surprises live.
bulletPoints: Flights and train tickets
Lunch and dinner, unless specifically mentioned
Entry fees at forts, churches and museums
Water sports and adventure activities — usually paid add-ons at the beach, even when the itinerary mentions them
Alcohol and personal expenses
The Dudhsagar jeep safari, unless it is written into the itinerary
GST and other applicable taxes
contentSections.highlightQuote: This list varies by operator. Ask for a written breakdown before you confirm anything.

contentSections.heading: Where you stay matters more in Goa than most places
contentSections.content: Budget stays are guesthouses and 2-star hotels, usually a short walk from the main beaches. Mid-range is 3-star with a pool and a better location, which is what most families take. Premium is the 4- and 5-star beach resorts, concentrated around Candolim, Sinquerim and South Goa. Beach access and the distance to nightlife or quiet change street by street here, so be specific about the kind of area you want rather than only the star rating.

contentSections.heading: Getting around
contentSections.content: Goa is compact and transport is one of the easier parts to plan. Private cabs for airport transfers and full-day sightseeing are the standard in an organised package. Self-drive scooters and bikes are popular with independent travellers but are not usually part of a package, and an Indian driving licence or an international permit is legally required. Ferries across the Mandovi and Zuari are a practical and scenic shortcut between some points. Ride-hailing apps work in the main tourist belts and are unreliable outside them. One thing worth clarifying before you travel: private transport in a package normally covers point-to-point sightseeing and transfers rather than being on call all day.

contentSections.heading: Who Goa suits, and what to book
contentSections.content: Couples do well with North Goa's beach resorts plus two quieter nights in the south — a good split between energy and downtime. Families are better off in a mid-range hotel near a calmer beach like Candolim or Colva, with a lighter sightseeing pace that leaves room for the pool. Friends and groups head for the Baga–Calangute belt, where nightlife, water sports and shared accommodation are easiest to arrange. First-time visitors get more out of a package that covers both halves, because Goa is a good deal more than the party image it carries.

contentSections.heading: Practical tips
contentSections.content: Six things worth knowing before you book.
bulletPoints: Book well ahead for November to February, especially Christmas and New Year
Carry sunscreen and light cotton clothing whatever the season
Water sports operators vary in safety standards — use the ones with visible licensing and life jackets
Check whether the hotel is on the beach or a few streets back; it changes both price and convenience
In the monsoon, confirm which shacks and activities are actually open before finalising anything
Carry cash for smaller vendors and the local markets

contentSections.heading: Common questions
contentSections.content: How many days are enough? Three to four for North Goa; at least five if you want South Goa as well. North or South for a first trip? Neither is objectively better — North for beaches, nightlife and markets, South for quiet beaches and resort stays, and both if time allows. A 2N/3D package is a North Goa weekend: hotel, breakfast, airport transfer, two or three beaches and one heritage or market stop, with no room for the south. A 3N/4D covers North Goa properly. A 4N/5D is the right length for both halves — two or three days north, one or two south, with a day for water sports or a cruise. Are water sports included? Generally no; they are paid add-ons at the beach even when the itinerary names them. Do packages include flights? Not usually, though they can be bundled in on request.
